seo.metaTitle: Create Random Noise PNG - Free Seeded Noise Generator
seo.metaDescription: Generate a random noise PNG where every pixel gets its own color, fixed by seed. Free, no upload, no signup, made and saved in your browser.
seo.longDescription: Random noise is an image in which every single pixel is given its own independent red, green and blue value, which is what produces television static, film grain and a flat test pattern. This page writes exactly that, over an opaque canvas with no transparency anywhere, and it needs no upload and no source file: the pixels are generated on your device and the result saved as PNG, JPG, WebP or BMP. Use it as a transparency test pattern, as a base texture to blend something over, or as an unpredictable-looking background. The Seed field is the part worth understanding - it is the starting number of the small random generator, so the same seed with the same canvas size always rebuilds the identical picture, which is how you get a repeatable noise texture rather than a new one on every visit. It is a reproducibility control, not a security feature.
howTo: No upload needed - the pixels are generated from the Canvas size and the Seed.
Set the Canvas size in pixels, or pick a preset; the noise fills every pixel.
Set the Seed from 0 to 999999999 to choose which noise field you get.
Change the seed again to jump to a completely different noise field.
Download the result as PNG, JPG, WebP or BMP from the Download button.

faq.q: What exactly does the seed do?
faq.a: It seeds the pseudo-random generator that picks the color of each pixel. The same seed with the same canvas size gives byte-for-byte the same image every time; a different seed gives a completely unrelated field. It is not encryption and it is not a password.

No. Every pixel is written fully opaque, so the result has no alpha channel at all even though it is saved as a PNG. If you want grain added to an existing picture instead, use the add noise tool on this site.

faq.q: How is this different from random color blocks?
faq.a: Here every pixel is independent, which reads as static or grain. Random color blocks gives each square of a chosen size a single flat color, which reads as a mosaic. Pick noise for fine grain and blocks for a chunky pattern.

faq.q: Is there any limit on size or any upload?
faq.a: No upload and no account. The canvas runs from 1 to 5000 pixels per side, and very large canvases take a moment because every pixel is written - a 5000 by 5000 canvas is 25 million pixels.
